sections.title: Loss and Return
sections.description: Naomi loses her family and returns to Bethlehem with Ruth

sections.title: The Gleaning
sections.description: Ruth gleans grain in Boaz's field

sections.title: The Threshing Floor
sections.description: Ruth visits Boaz on the threshing floor

sections.title: Redemption
sections.description: Boaz redeems Ruth, and the family line continues

events.title: Famine
events.description: A famine strikes Bethlehem. Elimelek takes his wife Naomi and their two sons Mahlon and Kiljon to Moab. There Elimelek dies, and the sons marry Moabite women, Orpa and Ruth. After ten years, both sons also die.
events.year_display: In the time of the judges

events.title: Ruth's vow of loyalty
events.description: Naomi decides to return to Judah. She asks her daughters-in-law to stay in Moab. Orpah turns back, but Ruth refuses to leave her: 'Where you go, I will go, and where you live, I will live. Your people shall be my people, and your God my God.'
events.year_display: In the time of the judges

events.title: Arrival in Bethlehem
events.description: Naomi and Ruth arrive in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest. The whole town is moved, and Naomi says they should call her Mara, for the Almighty has made life bitter for her.
events.year_display: In the time of the judges

events.title: Ruth Gleans in Boaz's Field
events.description: Ruth goes out to glean and ends up by chance in the field of Boaz, a relative of Elimelech. Boaz notices her and orders his servants to let her gather freely and even to pull some grain from the sheaves for her.
events.year_display: In the time of the judges

events.title: Boaz Shows Kindness
events.description: Ruth returns to Naomi with an ephah of barley. Naomi tells that Boaz is one of their kinsmen-redeemers and praises the Lord's goodness. Ruth continues to glean in Boaz's field throughout the barley and wheat harvest.
events.year_display: In the time of the judges

events.title: Ruth at the threshing floor
events.description: Naomi instructs Ruth to go to the threshing floor at night and lie down at Boaz's feet. She asks him to spread his cloak over her, as a sign that he is their kinsman-redeemer. Boaz praises her loyalty and promises to settle the matter.
events.year_display: In the time of the judges

events.title: Boaz negotiates at the city gate
events.description: Boaz goes to the city gate and gathers ten elders of the town as witnesses. The nearest kinsman-redeemer is willing to buy Naomi's land, but withdraws when he learns that he must also marry Ruth to carry on the name of the deceased. The redeemer removes his sandal as a sign that he gives up his right.
events.year_display: In the time of the judges

events.title: Boaz marries Ruth; Obed is born
events.description: Boaz takes Ruth as his wife, and the Lord enables her to conceive. She gives birth to a son who is named Obed. The women of the town praise the Lord for Naomi, and Naomi becomes the child's foster mother.
events.year_display: In the time of the judges

events.title: Obed's lineage to David
events.description: The closing genealogy of the book traces the line from Perez through Boaz and Obed to Jesse and his son David, thus linking Ruth's story to the kingdom of Israel.
events.year_display: In the time of the judges
